method: Independent manual reading of all 16 complete authoritative policy bodies and all 64 inputs, expected outcomes, quoted evidence, rationales and paired boundaries/exclusions. Structural hash, exact-quote, support-token, role and topic/aggregate checks supplement that reading; authoring tests and generated outputs weren't used as an oracle.

per_case_assessments.reason: The changed durable publisher needs actual interruption, restart and recovery evidence under FAIL-1 through FAIL-3.
A mocked happy path leaves the claimed crash recovery unverified, so requiring changes follows the runtime-failure rules.
The help-heading edit leaves executable behavior unchanged, so this policy needn't be selected.
The revised input changes publisher recovery and supplies runtime failure/restart/retry evidence; the boundary limits SSDF claims rather than excluding changed recovery.
A changed producer response and strict installed consumer belong to the public serialization contract.
An internal dictionary test can't establish acceptance by the rejecting installed consumer.
A private variable rename with unchanged exported behavior doesn't create a new public contract.
The revised optional public field selects the policy; supported old/new shapes and malformed-ID rejection supply offline contract evidence without a semantic or live-quality claim.
An exposed API change needs compatibility and consumer evidence under the declared version contract.
Replacing an object with a list breaks the declared consumer contract and needs a supported migration.
A private helper change leaves the published API contract unchanged.
A compatible optional addition can retain its version when consumer compatibility is demonstrated; SemVer isn't imposed on HTTP paths.
An HTTP error response and its caller recovery behavior fall within the safe error contract.
Credential-bearing error details and treating denied authorization as transient violate safe disclosure and recovery rules.
An unchanged successful display doesn't modify the error contract.
An existing safe documented error representation can remain; RFC 9457 adoption is optional.
An authorized collection cursor needs ownership, ordering, bounds and termination behavior.
A cursor crossing tenant ownership or failing to terminate violates the documented collection contract.
A scalar operation without collection behavior falls outside pagination requirements.
A fixed small collection can omit pagination within the documented bounded-collection exception.
A changing stored representation and rollout need compatibility, progress and actual recovery evidence.
Dropping the old column strands old readers and an untested backup doesn't verify restore; the verdict is supported, with a rationale reference correction recorded separately.
A read-only query change leaves stored representations and migration behavior unchanged.
Engine-specific transaction and recovery behavior needs an explicit workload decision; the policy supplies no universal numeric recovery target.
Coupled writes and effects need the declared atomic boundary and interruption/retry verification.
Separate commits can split debit and credit, and database rollback can't undo a sent external payment.
An unchanged read-only display doesn't create a multi-effect transaction.
An outbox can be used with its own atomicity and delivery proof; the PostgreSQL example doesn't mandate adopting that engine.
Durable background work needs duplicate-effect handling, bounded retries and observable terminal behavior.
Repeated charging after a lost acknowledgment and an unbounded poison retry violate job effect and retry rules.
A local pure calculation without a queue, durable job or external effect falls outside this job policy.
A documented harmless repeat can be acceptable when its safety is demonstrated; exactly-once execution isn't universally required.
An enabled security-sensitive service needs validated required configuration before accepting work.
Accepting requests before validating a required issuer violates the explicit startup requirement.
A static contact-detail edit leaves configuration and startup behavior unchanged.
A disabled optional integration may omit its credential, provided activation validates it first.
Dependent calls and retries need a shared deadline, safe retry admission and cancellation handling.
Independent endless retries multiply work beyond the deadline and cancellation boundary.
A pure calculation without dependency calls or retries doesn't trigger this policy.
Measured workload choices can determine timeouts; AWS example percentiles aren't universal project thresholds.
Admission under unequal resource costs needs bounded work, caller fairness and recovery evidence.
An unbounded queue and immediate amplified retries violate admission and caller behavior rules; the verdict is supported, with a rationale reference correction recorded separately.
A static dashboard layout change leaves admission, workload and overload behavior unchanged.
Unequal-cost work needs a cost-aware capacity account; aggregate request rate alone doesn't certify capacity.
A failed job with safe identifiers and absent secret markers falls within structured service-event logging.
Collecting personal data and raw user text without the approved exception violates default exclusion even when output is structured.
A static page layout edit doesn't change logging or private-data collection.
Avoiding sensitive collection is valid and preferred; JSON formatting alone doesn't establish privacy.
Queued retries and invalid inbound context need safe operation correlation and trace processing.
Discarding all correlation or inserting bearer credentials into trace state violates correlation and secret-handling requirements.
A pure helper rename without requests, workers, dependencies or telemetry changes falls outside this policy.
A child span can have a new span ID while retaining valid trace identity; repeating the parent span ID isn't required.
A missing index and validated replacement directly affect required local readiness capabilities.
Always-successful health hides unusable searches, and raw prompt labels expose private values with unbounded cardinality.
Incident-guide spelling changes leave probes, metrics and alerts unchanged.
Separate process liveness and data readiness responses match their different operational purposes.
A clean installed wheel, selected packs and locked dependencies fall within reviewed build-input and packaged-artifact evidence.
Unpinned tools, release credentials exposed to unreviewed code and checkout-only testing violate reviewed inputs and installed-artifact verification.
An unshipped meeting-agenda edit leaves build and distributed-artifact inputs unchanged.
Exact pins and platform records can be reported without claiming bit-for-bit reproducibility before rebuild evidence exists.
Consumer checks of authenticated identity, subject digest and altered bytes are within the verification policy.
Unsigned uploaded claims without consumer checking can't establish verified downloads.
Reordering local bookmarks without obtaining or trusting artifacts falls outside artifact verification.
Selected digest and provenance checks can be reported without claiming a complete framework level or builder certification.

findings.issue: The rationale attributes exercised recovery to MIGRATE-1 and MIGRATE-3, while MIGRATE-2 explicitly requires real-reader recovery verification.
findings.requested_change: Name MIGRATE-1 and MIGRATE-2 for compatibility and exercised recovery, or name all three if irreversible deletion is discussed.

findings.issue: The rationale attributes bounded admission and caller behavior to OVERLOAD-1 and OVERLOAD-3. Caller fairness and amplification avoidance are OVERLOAD-2; OVERLOAD-3 covers saturation, cancellation, release and recovery tests.
findings.requested_change: Name OVERLOAD-1 and OVERLOAD-2 for the described admission and retry behavior.

targeted_primary_section_checks.assessment: The narrowed mappings concern security testing, reviewed components and integrity information; general reliability and installed-artifact project rules remain labeled.
The listed controls address untrusted metadata/code, dependency tooling/documentation and authenticated release integrity.
Status-code and Retry-After mappings are narrower than a general retry classification mandate; project retry choices remain labeled.
Trace and resource fields inform correlation and service identity. Project structured-event and severity rules aren't attributed to removed severity mappings.

reviewed_notices.assessment: Both OWASP-derived body footers retain adaptation wording consistent with their topic/aggregate grounding_kind, attribution, pinned upstream URLs, CC-BY-SA-4.0 terms and change notices. All seven engineering notices now preserve that labeling. Existing upstream and CC-BY-SA notice files remain present; this checks internal attribution consistency rather than legal sufficiency.

diff_assessment.two_boundary_inputs: Both now change the runtime or public serialization behavior that selects their policy. Out-of-scope inputs and all expected verdicts remain unchanged.
diff_assessment.per_policy_sections: Body footers, rule support tokens and topic/aggregate source records were reviewed; broad unused SSDF/OSPS/HTTP/OpenTelemetry section lists were narrowed.
diff_assessment.historical_evidence: Documentation marks prior receipts and the current generation/bundle as historical pending independent review and rebuild. No previous model result was relabeled.

limits: This reviews the authored source expectations, not model selection, retrieval recall, generated answers, runtime compliance or production readiness.
All 64 cases are authored expectations; none was executed against a provider during this review.

External primary-source checking was targeted to the changed SSDF, OSPS, RFC 9110 and pinned OpenTelemetry mappings. This isn't an exhaustive review of all external frameworks or their complete requirements.
Quoted requirements are policy source evidence. Their fidelity doesn't establish correct applicability to every future task.
This isn't a legal opinion, license certification or framework compliance certification.

The receipt binds only the stated source and semantic payload. Corrections to either rationale require a new payload binding; unchanged source/outcome assessments can be carried forward with an explicit delta review.
